audit_findings.title: The anchor may omit the full run-rate interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.154 million pre-tax annualized interest gap: 2026 first-half interest of $6.416 million annualizes to $12.832 million versus $6.678 million in FY2025; the gap equals 23.6% of the $26.1 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE anchor retains interest expense, so projecting a partial-year financing charge overstates recurring OE and every scenario's operating PV.
audit_findings.evidence: On November 3, 2025, Pennant entered into the First Amendment to Amended and Restated Credit Agreement (the “First Amendment”), which provides for an incremental term loan credit facility (the “Incremental Term Loans”) in an aggregate principal amount of $ 100,000 (the “Incremental Term Loans”).
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch, not merely a possible debt-principal issue. The late-2025 financing burden is materially larger in the 2026 results. Using the supplied base PV-to-anchor ratio, the pre-tax gap corresponds to about $86.5 million, or $2.16 per share, before recognizing the tax shield. Full-year acquired earnings may offset some or all of this reduction, but they must be measured on the same perimeter.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct trailing-twelve-month OE through June 2026 using the filed interest expense, then rerun all scenarios with full-period acquired earnings and financing costs measured together.

audit_findings.title: NCI leakage could mix consolidated cash flows with the parent-share claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated D&A, capital expenditure, working-capital adjustments and bridge assets may include subsidiary amounts belonging to NCI holders even though OE begins with income attributable to Pennant and value is divided only among Pennant shares.
audit_findings.evidence: The acquisition includes 67 % ownership in a joint venture.
audit_findings.explanation: The potential mismatch remains unresolved. The filings show $45.239 million of NCI equity at June 2026 and $3.590 million of NCI income for the first half, but neither amount measures the actual leakage in OE or the bridge. D&A and cash leakage would generally overstate value, while consolidated capital expenditure or working-capital deductions could offset it.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the subsidiary-level OE reconciliation and ownership schedule; assign every D&A, capex, working-capital and bridge-cash amount to Pennant's economic percentage and rerun if the parent-only totals differ.

audit_findings.title: Unsettled acquisition consideration may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.387 million purchase-price reduction, approximately $0.01 per diluted share and 0.09% of the $410 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A residual seller payable would enter the equity bridge as a senior claim, but the final settlement instead reduced purchase consideration and goodwill.
audit_findings.evidence: The purchase price is subject to further adjustment based on final working capital and other closing considerations to be determined following the transaction’s close.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q states that final working-capital and other closing considerations were agreed and reduced the purchase price by $0.387 million. That resolves the provisional item in the supplied record, and its scale is immaterial relative to the base valuation.
audit_findings.action: No valuation rerun is needed; retain the final settlement documentation and confirm the acquisition ledger contains no residual seller payable or contingent consideration.

audit_findings.title: Medicare reviews create potentially unreserved recoupment claims
audit_findings.mechanism: Unreserved repayments would reduce future OE or enter the equity bridge as claims senior to common equity; reversals of previously recognized revenue would also lower the OE base.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, 12 of the Company’s independent operating subsidiaries had Reviews scheduled, on appeal or in dispute resolution process, both pre- and post-payment.
audit_findings.explanation: The uncertainty has increased rather than resolved: subsidiaries under Review rose from 12 at December 2025 to 16 at June 2026. The $3.796 million filed refunds-payable balance does not identify the amount reserved for these Reviews, and the filings cannot quantify possible denials, extrapolation, penalties or payment suspension. The record therefore cannot establish materiality, despite a potentially material downside path.
audit_findings.action: Obtain a review-by-review schedule of claims tested, denial rates, amounts appealed, extrapolation populations, payments suspended and reserves recorded; rerun OE and the bridge for any probable exposure not already recognized.

audit_findings.title: Known 2026 reimbursement pressure may invalidate nonnegative growth assumptions
audit_findings.mechanism: Company-specific reimbursement pressure would reduce OE margins and may require lower near-term growth than the valuation's 0%, 3% and 6% assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2026 HH Payment Final Rule’s net payment update percentage is -1.3%, resulting in an aggregate estimated decrease across all home health providers of $220 million in payments compared to fiscal year 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The pressure is already observable but its OE effect is not isolated. The filed 2026 first-half Medicare home-health revenue per completed episode fell $55, or 1.5%, and the second-quarter decline was $72, or 1.9%. Strong admission growth and hospice reimbursement may offset the rate decline, so the aggregate $220 million industry reduction cannot be assigned to Pennant from this record.
audit_findings.action: Build a company-specific 2026 reimbursement bridge using Medicare home-health revenue, episodes, payer mix, wage-index and case-mix changes, labor inflation and cost offsets; compare the resulting OE growth with each scenario and rerun any unsupported case.

audit_findings.title: Temporary state relief remains embedded in reported earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.743 million pretax in FY2025, equal to 6.7% of the $26.1 million anchor; approximately $1.290 million after the filed 26.0% tax rate and about $0.45 per share of base-value sensitivity
audit_findings.mechanism: Relief recorded as a reduction of cost of services increases reported earnings and OE if the normalization did not remove it.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company recognized state relief funding totaling $ 1,743 and $ 3,331 , respectively, which the Company recognized as a reduction of cost of services.
audit_findings.explanation: Even assuming the entire FY2025 amount remains in the anchor and is nonrecurring, the computed after-tax sensitivity is about 4.9% of anchor OE and 4.4% of the $10.23 base value per share. The roughly $0.45 per-share effect is small relative to the $27.77 gap between the base value and the $38 market price, so it does not change the valuation conclusion. Continued recognition of $0.807 million in the first half of 2026 also shows that the benefit did not immediately disappear.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE workpaper to confirm whether relief was normalized; if retained, run a disclosure sensitivity excluding the $1.743 million FY2025 amount and continue tracking the program's 2026 receipts and eligibility.
